subject: Reliability regression: executive brief + action roster
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, James Carter <james.carter@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Incident detected: inference latency regression affecting Acme Analytics

Team,

We detected a sustained latency regression in the hosted inference path serving Acme Analytics between 08:45–09:05 UTC this morning. Impact summary:~15% of requests to the customer’s production model experienced p50 latency increases from ~95ms to ~420ms; p99 degraded to ~2.1s. This pushed their SLA for the day below the committed 99.9%.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Rolled traffic to a smaller instance pool and enabled auto-burst (temporary).
- Disabled a new kernel selection optimization rolled earlier this week (PR #542).
- Restarted affected inference nodes in region-us-west1.

Attachments: incident_timeline.csv (sampled traces + node metrics).

Requesting: quick exec readout for QBR inclusion and confirmation of owner for customer communications. James — we’ve looped you so you’re aware; we’ll propose a remediation cadence.

Hannah
SVP, Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Incident detected: inference latency regression affecting Acme Analytics

Thanks Hannah — quick executive summary for the QBR / leadership notes:
- Incident type: regression introduced by a kernel selection change that mismatched on long-sequence workloads (suspected scheduling edge case).
- Severity: SLA exception for Acme (single-day breach). No data exfiltration; customer requests live are rate-limited and integrity preserved.
- Current state: mitigations in place, traffic stabilized, root cause analysis in progress.

Action asked of leadership:
1) Approve a temporary SLA credit to Acme while we complete the runbook and RCAs (Marissa to compute).
2) Greenlight a small rollback window for the kernel change candidate while we complete regression tests (Karthik to coordinate).
3) Include a 1-slide summary in QBR that notes impact, remediation, and action owners — Neha, can you confirm this slide will be ready by Monday?

Date: 2027-06-20T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Incident detected: inference latency regression affecting Acme Analytics

Acknowledged. Quick notes from the postmortem drafts:
- Root cause: a kernel selector heuristic misapplied to sequences >1024 tokens when combined with contiguous KV cache access patterns. The optimization flagged previously unseen hot-path scheduling thrash on our cuda stream pool.
- Why it escaped tests: test suite focussed on short and max-length extremes but not on the mid-tail distribution that Acme exercises (heavy 600–900 token median).
- Permanent remediation plan:
  * tighten kernel selector thresholds and add a load-aware probe (Karthik — will submit patch).
  * expand CI generation to include sampled production loads (Jonas to own).
  * add an early-detection SLO alert for median shift + p99 tail height (Hannah).

Added action (requested): open INF JIRA (INF-1234) and flag as P1; attach runbook_patch.diff to the ticket. Also recommend filing a short SLA exception request document for legal/accounting — I can draft.

- Add production-median monitoring and p99 tail alerting to reduce recurrence risk (Hannah owner).
